ref: Architecture C — per-client effective thresholds
problem: The brief scopes effectiveThresholds threading to the engine only ('thread through analyzeClient/analyzeAd/etc'), but creative.ts diagnose() and nextBatchPlan() read THRESHOLDS as T at 9 sites (creative.ts:61,67,73,78,84,89,137,138) and judge the SAME per-client signals the engine does: minSpendVsCPA, minImpressionsToJudge, fatigueFrequency, fatigueCtrDropWoW, hookRateFloor, holdRateFloor, cvrFloor, minPurchasesToJudge. creativePerformance/nextBatchPlan are called per-client from CreativeLab.tsx:34,36, ClientDashboard.tsx:44, and report.ts:68. If overrides reach the engine but not creative.ts, a client tuned 'aggressive' will see contradictory fatigue/winner calls between the Recommendations feed and the Creative Lab for the same ad — a visible honesty gap.
recommendation: Thread the resolved thresholds into creative.ts too: creativePerformance(ds, clientId, range) already has clientId, so resolve effectiveThresholds(clientId) at its top and pass into diagnose() and nextBatchPlan() exactly as the engine does. Scope this into Wave 2 alongside the engine change; do NOT let creative.ts keep the bare global import. NOTE diagnose() also hardcodes a 0.9 CPA-winner ratio (creative.ts:89) that is NOT in THRESHOLDS and mirrors the engine's scaleCpaRatio (0.8) — decide whether per-client tuning should reach it or leave it fixed, but document the choice.

ref: Architecture A — ConfigStore vs the existing single config home
problem: The brief introduces a NEW `ConfigStore` holding `ClientConfig` (per-client targets) as a parallel store, but every existing consumer resolves client targets from ONE place: the `Client` objects in the snapshot's embedded Dataset — `snapshot.clientById.get(...)` / `snapshot.clients` — read by the engine (engine.ts:60 `client.targetCPA`, :249, :265-267 monthlyBudget/targetCPA), report.ts:50,94, creative.ts:40,150,163, llm.ts, and ~10 screens (Campaigns.tsx:124, ClientDashboard.tsx:52,83, PortfolioOverview.tsx:128-129, ClientsDirectory.tsx:62, CreativeLab.tsx:52, WeeklyReportScreen.tsx:189, ScopeSwitcher.tsx:82, Overview.tsx). If ConfigStore overrides live alongside the untouched snapshot Client, any screen/engine path that forgets to merge reads STALE seeded targets — a direct violation of the v1 'screens + engine read the same source' invariant.
recommendation: Make ConfigStore the persistence layer but NOT a second read source. On snapshot load (store.init / applyProviderMode), hydrate ConfigStore and apply overrides ONTO the snapshot's `Client` objects (the single home) via one resolver `applyClientConfig(client, cfg): Client` — so `snapshot.clientById` already carries effective targets and ALL existing consumers stay correct with zero edits. This mirrors how `loadThresholds()` already mutates the global THRESHOLDS in place before the first pass (store.ts:94). Editing targets in Settings should both persist via ConfigStore AND re-apply onto the in-memory Client + bumpSnapshot, exactly like setThreshold does (store.ts:205-210).

ref: Architecture A — ClientConfig vs LiveConfig.clients (two competing homes)
problem: `LiveConfig.clients: Client[]` (liveProvider.ts:67-74) already exists as the documented home for 'clients metadata (targets etc.) the API doesn't carry — set in Settings', and SettingsScreen.tsx:43 already writes `clients: snapshot.clients` into it. The brief's new `ClientConfig` (partial, by clientId) overlaps this directly. Shipping both creates two persisted client-target homes that can disagree (one live-only keyed by `meridian.live.config`, one new keyed by `meridian.config`).
recommendation: Pick ONE seam. Recommended: keep ConfigStore as the single per-client targets+overrides store (mode-agnostic, applies in BOTH demo and live), and in live mode source `LiveConfig.clients` FROM ConfigStore at provider-build time rather than persisting a duplicate Client[] in Settings. Delete/redirect the `clients: snapshot.clients` write at SettingsScreen.tsx:43 so live config stops being a second target home. Document this in the seam: ConfigStore is the home; LiveConfig.clients is a derived projection for the live provider.

ref: Architecture A — async Promise signatures vs synchronous selectors
problem: The brief specifies `ConfigStore.load(): Promise<...>` and `HistoryStore.forEntity(): Promise<DecisionRecord[]>`. But the entire UI reads state synchronously: `useSnapshot()` returns a value (hooks.ts:6-13) and every engine call is a sync `useMemo(() => analyzeScope(snapshot, scope), …)` (Recommendations.tsx:39-45, Campaigns.tsx:33, PortfolioOverview.tsx:53, ClientDashboard.tsx:43). You cannot `await store.forEntity()` inside a sync useMemo or inside `analyzeClient`. If the drawer reads history via an awaited Promise it's fine (effect-driven), but threading effective-config through the sync engine via an async load is not.
recommendation: Keep the async seam interface (backend-swap honesty) but HYDRATE once into synchronous zustand state during init/provider-swap: `await configStore.load()` in store.init, then hold `clientConfig: Record<string,ClientConfig>` in state and apply onto the snapshot. The engine never awaits — it reads the already-merged Client. History: the drawer/Activity view load via Promise in a useEffect (fine, async-tolerant); recording at decision time is fire-and-forget (see next). Document explicitly that 'async at the seam, sync in the selector path via a one-time hydrate' is the contract.

ref: Theme 1 — unique entity name on SuggestionCard
problem: Ad names are confirmed non-unique: generate.ts:379 builds them as `${creative.angle} · ${creative.format} · ${creative.batch}` (e.g. 'UGC Testimonial · video · Batch A'), and the same creative is sampled across multiple ad sets (generate.ts:354,360), so identical ad names recur across the tree. AdSet names (generate.ts:343) can also collide across campaigns. The entityId is always unique, but a user reading the card sees only the name. The brief floats 'append adset? a vN?' as an open question.
recommendation: Disambiguate by parent path, not a synthetic vN. Show the parent path (ad → 'AdSet name · Campaign name'; adset → 'Campaign name') resolved via adById→adSetById→campaignById (generate.ts:80-82). The vN idea is wrong here — names already contain a vN-ish token ('v1') from the CREATIVE, not the ad, so a second vN would mislead. Parent path is the honest disambiguator and is also what the drawer header needs, so build the resolver once (a `parentPath(snapshot, level, entityId)` selector) and reuse it on both the card and the drawer.

ref: Theme 1 — surfacing entity when showClient=false
problem: SuggestionCard hides entityName ONLY inside the `showClient && client` block (SuggestionCard.tsx:79-86), so in client-scoped contexts (Recommendations with scope.kind==='client' → SuggestionCard.tsx... Recommendations.tsx:139; ClientDashboard.tsx:183; WeeklyReportScreen.tsx:203) the entity name AND the level are both hidden. The brief correctly flags this. The risk in the fix is redundancy: when showClient=true the client avatar+name already renders, and the entity name sits beside it — adding a parent path that repeats the client is noise.
recommendation: Restructure the card to always render a level chip + entity name + parent path in its own row, independent of showClient. Make showClient control ONLY the client avatar/name affordance. When client-scoped (showClient=false), the parent path should stop at campaign (never repeat the client, which is already the page context); when portfolio/bm-scoped, the client avatar carries the client and the parent path stays campaign-level. This avoids both the hidden-entity bug and client-name redundancy.

ref: Honesty Firewall #2 + ledger schema (DecisionRecord.outcome)
problem: The firewall is internally inconsistent about what the ledger shows in demo. Firewall #2 says any demo outcome score is 'illustrative/simulated and labeled as such,' but the schema comment says outcome 'may be null forever in demo,' and L5 says 'demo-illustrative.' These are two different product behaviors: (a) outcome stays null and the UI shows 'awaiting live data,' vs (b) a simulated/labeled outcome is shown. Given the verified frozen-time reality (today()=DATA_TODAY metrics.ts:111; demoProvider writes no post-action insights demoProvider.ts:20-57), a 'simulated' outcome in demo would be a fabricated number with no data basis — exactly the 'faked it worked' the firewall forbids.
recommendation: Lock ONE demo behavior: outcome stays null/absent in demo and the drawer+ledger render an explicit 'Outcome: pending — measured on live data over elapsed time' state. Drop the word 'illustrative/simulated' for outcomes entirely (it invites a fabricated number); reserve 'illustrative' only for clearly non-numeric explanatory copy. Make outcome strictly null in demo a tested invariant.

ref: Wave 1 risk classification (per-client targets / ConfigStore + effectiveClient)
problem: The brief labels W1 'low risk' and targets 'easy,' but the engine and 8 screens read client.targetCPA/targetROAS/monthlyBudget/avgOrderValue directly off the snapshot Client object at ~20 sites (engine.ts:60,249,265,267,279,282; report.ts; ClientDashboard.tsx:52,65,83; PortfolioOverview.tsx:128-129; CreativeLab.tsx:52; ScopeSwitcher.tsx:82). There is NO effectiveClient/config-resolution layer today (grep for effectiveClient/ClientConfig/ConfigStore returns nothing). So W1 cannot ship per-client targets without either (a) mutating the memoized snapshot Client objects on config load — entangling with the dataset lifecycle and demo/live swap — or (b) threading an effectiveClient(clientId,config) resolver through the same engine read sites the brief reserves for W2's threshold refactor. Either way W1 touches the engine; it is the FIRST persistence seam and the first engine read-path change, not a UI-only surfacing task.
recommendation: Reclassify W1 as medium risk and give it the same guardrails the brief grants W2: add P0 cases proving identical engine output when no client config exists, before wiring the editor. Decide the resolution strategy explicitly in the pack — strongly prefer an effectiveClient() resolver (pure, testable, mirrors the planned effectiveThresholds()) over snapshot mutation, because mutation collides with the documented shallow-clone/by-reference snapshot contract in store.ts:229-235 and the provider-swap reset.

ref: Architecture C — interface choice (context vs lookup)
problem: The brief offers 'EngineContext { thresholds }' OR 'a resolved thresholds arg' as equivalent. They are not equal in blast radius. analyzeAd is the EXPORTED test surface (engineBehavior.test.ts:60,69 calls analyzeAd(ds, ad, client) with a 3-arg signature). Adding a required 4th positional thresholds arg breaks that test signature; an EngineContext object passed as a new positional also breaks it. A per-call-site effectiveThresholds(clientId) lookup inside analyzeAd would re-resolve (and re-spread) on every ad — wasteful and it loses the single-resolution guarantee.
recommendation: Resolve ONCE in analyzeClient: const t = effectiveThresholds(clientId, config). Pass t as an OPTIONAL trailing param: analyzeAd(ds, ad, client, t: typeof THRESHOLDS = THRESHOLDS). Default = the live global THRESHOLDS so the existing 3-arg test calls and behavior stay byte-identical with zero test edits. Same optional-trailing-arg pattern for analyzeAdSets/analyzeReallocation/analyzePacing/analyzeAnomalies. This is the concrete recommended approach — not a context object.

ref: Architecture C + store.ts setThreshold coexistence
problem: Global sliders mutate THRESHOLDS by reference (thresholds.ts:81 setThreshold; thresholds.ts:74 loadThresholds Object.assign) and the store re-derives via bumpSnapshot (store.ts:205-215). If effectiveThresholds captures a COPY of THRESHOLDS at module load or memoizes it, a global slider change will no longer flow into per-client resolution — the base layer goes stale. Merge precedence is also unstated: is the per-client preset applied before or after explicit thresholdOverrides, and does a global slider edit override a per-client value or sit beneath it?
recommendation: effectiveThresholds must read the LIVE THRESHOLDS object at call time (resolve inside analyzeClient, invoked fresh each analysis pass — it already is, since screens re-run analyzeScope on each [snapshot] bump). Lock precedence as: base = live global THRESHOLDS (slider-editable default) -> preset delta -> explicit per-client thresholdOverrides (most specific wins). Document that a global slider moves the BASE for every client that has not overridden that specific key. Re-scoring per client must also bump the snapshot/version (the existing bumpSnapshot path) so config edits re-derive screens exactly like slider edits do today (store.ts:209).

ref: Wave 2 verification / P0 suite
problem: The brief says 'P0 suite must stay green + add per-client cases' but does not specify the proving tests, and the determinism test (engine.test.ts:36) only guarantees same-build reproducibility, not identical-with-vs-without-config. Nothing currently proves the no-override path is byte-identical or that an override actually re-scores.
recommendation: Add three tests: (a) IDENTICAL — analyzeScope(ds,scope) with config={} (or no config arg) deep-equals the current output (snapshot the suggestion array: id/type/severity/confidence/title); the optional-default-arg design makes this pass with zero source edits to existing assertions. (b) RE-SCORES — set a client's cutCpaRatio override low enough to flip a specific ad from no-suggestion to CUT_BUDGET and assert the new suggestion appears for THAT client only. (c) ISOLATION — overriding client A does not change any suggestion for client B in the same analyzeScope pass. Mirror (a)/(b) for creative.ts diagnose() once it is threaded.

ref: Architecture C — effectiveThresholds threading vs the existing module-global pattern
problem: The brief proposes threading `EngineContext { thresholds }` through `analyzeClient`/`analyzeAd`/etc. instead of importing global `T`. But `THRESHOLDS as T` is a MODULE import in TWO files (engine.ts:16 AND creative.ts:11), the engine has 7 analysis functions (`analyzeAd`, `analyzeAdSets`, `analyzeReallocation`, `analyzePacing`, `analyzeAnomalies`, `analyzeClient`, `analyzeScope`) plus `analyzeCreatives`/`generateReport`, and the P0 test calls `analyzeAd(ds, ad, client)` with a fixed 3-arg signature (engineBehavior.test.ts:60,69). A full signature thread is a wide, test-breaking refactor — exactly the destabilization the kill criterion (L6) guards against.
recommendation: Prefer the lowest-blast-radius option that the codebase already demonstrates: resolve per-client effective thresholds at the `analyzeClient` boundary (it already looks up the client at engine.ts:351) and pass a single resolved `thresholds` object DOWN to the per-ad/per-set helpers as one added param with a default of global `T` (so `analyzeAd(ds, ad, client, t = T)` keeps existing 3-arg test calls green). Do NOT also refactor creative.ts in Wave 2 unless threshold overrides actually affect creative diagnosis — scope it. Add the 'identical with no overrides' golden test BEFORE the refactor, per the kill criterion. Flag in the prompt-pack that this is the single riskiest edit in v2.

ref: Architecture C — 'Breakeven ROAS already wired' honesty gap
problem: The brief says breakeven 'feed[s] the LLM context, already wired' (line 122). In reality `breakevenRoas` is DECLARED and CONSUMED in llm.ts:34-55 but PRODUCED by nothing — a repo-wide grep for any code setting `breakevenRoas:` returns zero producers. The LLM context field is dangling; no path computes `1/contributionMargin` and assigns it. Building Wave 1 on the assumption it's wired will surface a no-op.
recommendation: Treat breakeven as NEW work in Wave 1, not surfacing-only: add a single `breakevenRoas(client) = 1 / client.contributionMargin` helper (guard margin>0), wire it into the LLM context builder (wherever LLMContext is assembled) and into the screens/report that judge ROAS. Correct the brief line 122 to 'breakeven ROAS is a NEW derived value (consumer stub exists in llm.ts; no producer yet)'.

ref: Architecture A — HistoryStore recording hook + relation to existing state
problem: The brief asks recording to happen at decision time but doesn't reconcile with the store's existing `applied`/`appliedSuggestionIds`/`dismissedSuggestionIds` (store.ts:46-49,89), which are session-only Sets that are RESET on every provider swap (store.ts:111-113) and never persisted. The ledger overlaps these but must NOT replace the dedup Sets the live feed depends on (Recommendations.tsx:42 filters on them) — and it must capture pre-metrics, which `applySuggestion` does not currently compute (it only captures status/budget via captureRestore, store.ts:151).
recommendation: Record in `applySuggestion` (store.ts:137) and `dismissSuggestion` (store.ts:189) as an ADDITIVE fire-and-forget `void historyStore.record(...)` — keep the existing Sets as the in-session dedup/feed source (they stay). The ledger is the durable, queryable record; the Sets are the live-feed working set. For `preMetrics`, compute the entity's current MetricsBundle at decision time via the existing `metricsForEntity`/`metricsForAdIds` selectors before applying (the snapshot is in hand in applySuggestion). Note the honesty firewall: in demo, snapshot is static so no real future exists — outcome stays null/illustrative (brief is correct here).

ref: Architecture A — localStorage key collision / mode-scoping
problem: The brief uses flat keys `meridian.config` and `meridian.history`. But provider mode swap resets session state because demo and live are different datasets/entity-id spaces (store.ts:104-115 comment: action sets 'key off the old dataset'). A single `meridian.history` ledger keyed by demo entityIds will mix with live entityIds after a flip, and demo decisions (simulated) would pollute a live ledger — an honesty-firewall concern (demo outcomes are illustrative only).
recommendation: Namespace persistence by provider mode (e.g. `meridian.history.demo` / `meridian.history.live`, same for config) OR stamp each DecisionRecord with `mode: 'demo'|'live'` and filter — so a demo's simulated, illustrative decisions never appear in a live accountability ledger. Decide this at the seam now; it's awkward to migrate later. ConfigStore is more defensibly mode-agnostic (targets are real intent), but history must be mode-segregated.

ref: Theme 1 — success metric #1 (account level)
problem: The brief repeatedly lists the level set as ad/ad set/campaign/account/client, but the engine never emits a suggestion at level:'account' (engine.ts only uses 'ad','adset','campaign','client' — see lines 75,216,250,268,306) and the Dataset has NO accountById index (generate.ts:64-86 only has accountByClient). adIdsForEntity DOES have an 'account' branch (selectors.ts:16-17) so metrics resolve, but resolving an account's NAME for the drawer header from an EntityRef requires a linear ds.accounts.find() scan (the same workaround liveProvider.ts:348 already does). So 'account' is a half-supported level: metrics work, name/header does not, and nothing ever opens it.
recommendation: Drop 'account' from the drawer's supported EntityRef levels for this initiative (the real hierarchy buyers click is campaign→adset→ad, plus client). If account must stay, add an accountById index to Dataset/generate.ts so the drawer header can resolve a name in O(1), and fix the success-metric copy to say 'ad/ad set/campaign/client'. Do NOT let the drawer ship a level that no surface opens and whose header can't render a name.

ref: Theme 2 — drawer vs the ?entity= deep-link
problem: The brief asks whether the drawer could replace or conflict with the Recommendations ?entity= deep-link (Recommendations.tsx:33-46, 74-86; opened from Campaigns.tsx:239 `Link to=/recommendations?entity=...`). They are NOT the same surface: the deep-link filters the recommendation LIST to one entityId and shows a 'Filtered to X' banner; the drawer is a global inspector that overlays the current screen. If a build prompt naively 'replaces the deep-link with the drawer', it would break the existing Campaigns spark→Recommendations flow and the shareable URL.
recommendation: Keep both, and make them compose: the drawer is store-state (ephemeral, not in the URL); the ?entity= filter stays URL-state (shareable/deep-linkable). The Campaigns sparkle Link can EITHER stay as-is OR be upgraded to open the drawer (drawer shows 'all recommendations for this entity', which is a superset of the filtered list) — but that's a UX choice, not a forced replacement. Explicitly instruct the prompt-pack NOT to move the drawer into the router/URL (the brief's 'opened from a single store field' is correct); a route would fight the existing scope+range+?entity= query state and lose the overlay-over-current-screen behavior.

ref: Theme 2 — EntityRef type does not exist yet
problem: The brief's drawer contract and the ConfigStore/HistoryStore schemas reference `EntityRef` and reuse `EntityLevel`/`SuggestionType`/`Severity` as if `EntityRef` exists. grep confirms EntityRef is NOT defined anywhere in src/ — it is net-new. The store (store.ts) has no `drawer` field. There is also NO existing drawer/modal/dialog/portal/focus-trap primitive in the codebase (primitives.tsx has none; grep for role=dialog/createPortal returns nothing), so the a11y slide-over is genuinely from-scratch, not a reuse.
recommendation: Wave 1/2 prompt must (a) define `export interface EntityRef { level: EntityLevel; entityId: string }` in types.ts and use it consistently across the drawer field, ConfigStore, and HistoryStore; (b) add `drawer: EntityRef | null` + `openDrawer/closeDrawer` actions to the store alongside the existing scope/range fields; (c) budget real effort for a net-new accessible slide-over (focus-trap, ESC, role=dialog, scroll-lock) since no primitive exists to extend — the brief's 'match-the-bar' design note assumes this is non-trivial and it is.

ref: Architecture C — effectiveThresholds vs the existing global-mutation threshold model
problem: The brief says the engine 'reads global THRESHOLDS by reference everywhere' and proposes threading EngineContext{thresholds} through analyzeClient/analyzeAd. But thresholds already have a runtime model that mutates the global THRESHOLDS object in place (thresholds.ts:80-88 setThreshold; store.ts:205-210 bumps the snapshot to re-derive). Per-client overrides break this global-singleton model fundamentally: you cannot have one global object hold per-client values. The brief's EngineContext approach is the correct fix, but it must also reconcile with / replace the existing global setThreshold path (Settings → global sliders), or you end up with two competing threshold-resolution mechanisms (global mutation + per-client merge) that can disagree.
recommendation: In the W2 design, make effectiveThresholds(clientId, config) the single resolution point: base = the (still-global, still-editable) THRESHOLDS, merged with config.thresholdOverrides/preset. Keep the global sliders as the base layer, per-client as the override layer, resolved in one function — and add a test that global-slider changes still take effect for clients with no override. Note this explicitly so the build doesn't leave the old by-reference mutation path as a hidden second source of truth.

ref: Wave 1 scope — Breakeven ROAS 'already wired'
problem: The brief's Architecture C says breakeven ROAS should 'feed the LLM context, already wired.' Only the CONSUMER is wired: llm.ts:36 declares breakevenRoas?: number and llm.ts:54-55 renders it in the prompt, but NOTHING computes or assigns breakevenRoas anywhere in the codebase (grep shows zero assignment sites; no code computes 1/contributionMargin despite the type comment at types.ts:48). So today the LLM always sees breakeven absent. The 'already wired' parenthetical overstates readiness and could cause W1 to skip the actual producer work.
recommendation: Scope breakeven ROAS in W1 as real (small) work: compute breakeven = 1/effectiveClient.contributionMargin in a shared helper, assign it into the llm.ts context builder's call site, and surface it in the targets editor + KPI strips. Correct the brief line to 'the LLM context FIELD exists; the value is not yet computed — wire the producer in W1.'

ref: Honesty Firewall #3 / Tier 2 calibration design
problem: The sample-guard + bounded + reversible + disclosed design is the right shape, but it is under-specified on the seam it persists through and on what 'reversible' means concretely. Calibration nudges per-client confidence/thresholds from realized hit-rate — that derived adjustment must be stored as its own layer (separate from the user's manual config overrides) so 'reversible' = drop the calibration layer without wiping the buyer's hand-set targets/overrides. The brief folds preset/thresholdOverrides and (implicitly) calibration into the same ClientConfig, which risks a silent merge where the buyer can't tell their value from the machine's.
recommendation: In the W3 Tier-2 design doc, make the calibration adjustment a distinct, separately-stored and separately-clearable layer (e.g. config.calibration with {key, delta, basis:{sampleN, hitRate}, appliedAt}) resolved AFTER manual overrides, and define the disclosure UI as 'engine nudged X by Y because Z (n=N) — revert.' Also define the min-sample N and the bound numerically in the doc so it isn't left to build-time guesswork. This stays design-only per L5.
